Docket 1.3.117

**Docket is free to try: run a full audit of any site without a key and see your score, how many problems each area has, and the most important problem in full with its fix. [Buy it once](https://kerr-affiliate-hub.kerrco.workers.dev/buy/docket?src=release-notes), $349, or 4 payments of $87.25, to see all the others, the ranked fix plan and the markup to paste. 30-day refund, no conditions.**

- *Structured data wrapped in an old CDATA comment is read, and the wrapper is reported plainly.* A complete block
  written the XHTML way, with //<![CDATA[ around it, was reported at high severity as data search engines throw away.
  Docket could not show that they do. The block is now read, and the wrapper is reported at medium severity: it is
  not valid JSON as written, some parsers strip it, others may discard the block, and removing it is free.
  Structured data that is broken in other ways is still reported at high severity.
- *Parts of one essay are no longer called rival pages.* An essay published as "Part 1 of 3", "Part 2 of 3" and
  "Part 3 of 3" was reported as pages competing for the same search, with advice to merge them. Pages that share a
  title and differ only by a part, chapter, episode or volume number are now read as one series. Yearly editions
  of a page, such as a 2024 and a 2025 list, are still reported as competing.
- *A "Download" link to a file is no longer called vague anchor text.* A podcast's "Download" link beside each
  episode, which hands over the episode's audio, was counted as non-descriptive, with advice to name the linked
  page's topic. A file is not a page, and "Download" is what the link does. A "download" link to an ordinary page
  is still reported.

99 checks across 13 areas.
